description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace" to hold all intermediate outputs.  
2. Obtain a recursive listing of every entry under /working and save it as "temp_workspace/listing.txt".  
3. From that listing, extract every path whose basename exactly equals "workspace" and save them to "temp_workspace/candidates.txt".  
4. For each path listed in "temp_workspace/candidates.txt", retrieve and record its file metadata (type and relevant attributes) into "temp_workspace/metadata.txt".  
5. Filter the recorded metadata to retain only entries that are regular files, writing those paths to "temp_workspace/regulars.txt".  
6. Confirm that each path in "temp_workspace/regulars.txt" is located within /working and append the confirmations to "temp_workspace/verified.txt".  
7. If multiple verified regular-file entries exist, record all duplicates in "temp_workspace/duplicates.txt" and designate the first canonical path as the primary candidate.  
8. Write the chosen primary candidate path (if any) into "temp_workspace/final_candidate.txt" and delete intermediate files that are not part of the final candidate or verification logs.  
9. Perform a consistency check by comparing "temp_workspace/final_candidate.txt" against "temp_workspace/listing.txt" and "temp_workspace/metadata.txt", and record the check outcome to "temp_workspace/check_result.txt".  
10. Prepare a one-line readiness summary in "temp_workspace/ready.txt" that states whether a verified regular file named "workspace" under /working exists, without emitting that result to the user.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace" to hold all intermediate artifacts and logs.  
2. Recursively obtain and save a complete listing of all filesystem entries under /working into "temp_workspace/all_entries.txt".  
3. From that listing, extract and save only entries whose basename equals "workspace" into "temp_workspace/matching_names.txt".  
4. For each path in "temp_workspace/matching_names.txt", obtain and record its file type and attributes (e.g., regular file, directory, symlink) into "temp_workspace/matching_attrs.txt".  
5. From "temp_workspace/matching_attrs.txt", produce "temp_workspace/regular_matches.txt" containing only paths identified as regular files.  
6. If "temp_workspace/regular_matches.txt" contains multiple paths, deterministically select and record a single canonical path into "temp_workspace/selected_match.txt"; if it contains one, copy that entry to "temp_workspace/selected_match.txt".  
7. Re-verify that the path in "temp_workspace/selected_match.txt" still exists and matches the recorded attributes, and if discrepancies are found update "temp_workspace/regular_matches_updated.txt" accordingly.  
8. Append a concise audit entry to "temp_workspace/audit.log" listing the number of candidate matches, verification steps performed, and the result of the re-check.  
9. Remove any intermediate files that are no longer needed while retaining "temp_workspace/regular_matches.txt", "temp_workspace/selected_match.txt", "temp_workspace/audit.log", and "temp_workspace/all_entries.txt" for traceability.  
10. Prepare a short summary file "temp_workspace/summary_for_output.txt" that presents the verification result (presence or absence) of a verified regular file named "workspace" under /working, leaving the final decision ready for output.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && mkdir /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a folder named "temp_workspace" to hold all intermediate artifacts for the check.  
2. Capture a recursive snapshot of the contents under /working and save it to "temp_workspace/initial_tree.txt".  
3. Extract all path entries named "workspace" from "temp_workspace/initial_tree.txt" and write them to "temp_workspace/matches_raw.txt".  
4. For each path listed in "temp_workspace/matches_raw.txt", determine its file type (regular file, directory, symlink, etc.) and record the results in "temp_workspace/matches_with_type.txt".  
5. Filter "temp_workspace/matches_with_type.txt" to retain only entries classified as regular files and save those to "temp_workspace/matches_regular.txt".  
6. Deduplicate "temp_workspace/matches_regular.txt" and write unique canonical paths to "temp_workspace/matches_unique.txt".  
7. For each path in "temp_workspace/matches_unique.txt", record its canonical absolute path plus basic metadata (size and permissions) into "temp_workspace/matches_meta.txt".  
8. Verify that none of the canonical paths in "temp_workspace/matches_meta.txt" are reachable only through broken or circular symlinks and record that verification in "temp_workspace/symlink_check.txt".  
9. Perform a consistency check comparing "temp_workspace/initial_tree.txt", "temp_workspace/matches_raw.txt", and "temp_workspace/matches_meta.txt" to confirm no modifications occurred during processing and save the result to "temp_workspace/sanity_check.txt".  
10. Aggregate the prepared evidence files into "temp_workspace/ready_to_report.txt", which lists the canonical regular-file paths found (if any) and marks the aggregated state as ready for a final existence decision.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/OS/workspace

description:
1. Create a temporary folder named "temp_workspace_check" to hold all intermediate artifacts and note that subsequent steps will use it.  
2. Record the existence and basic metadata of the directory /working into "temp_workspace_check/meta.txt".  
3. Recursively enumerate all entries under /working and save the raw list to "temp_workspace_check/all_entries.txt".  
4. Filter the raw list to retain only entries whose final name is exactly "workspace" and save those paths to "temp_workspace_check/matches_raw.txt".  
5. For each path in matches_raw.txt, obtain and record the path's file type and permission metadata into "temp_workspace_check/matches_info.txt".  
6. From matches_info.txt, extract only those entries explicitly identified as regular files and write them to "temp_workspace_check/regular_matches.txt".  
7. Normalize and deduplicate the paths in regular_matches.txt and save the result as "temp_workspace_check/regular_unique.txt".  
8. Perform a consistency check comparing regular_unique.txt against all_entries.txt and record any inconsistencies to "temp_workspace_check/discrepancies.txt".  
9. Remove intermediate files that are no longer needed, preserving only meta.txt, regular_unique.txt, and discrepancies.txt in temp_workspace_check.  
10. Create a concise pre-decision summary file "temp_workspace_check/decision_ready.txt" that contains the count of entries in regular_unique.txt and marks this summary as the final pre-check artifact to be used when producing the final answer.

If a regular file named "workspace" exists in /working (recursively)? If so, output "yes", otherwise output "no" (with out quotes).

create.init: rm -rf /working; mkdir /working && echo 123>/working/.tmp && echo 123>/working/.tm12p && echo 123>/working/.f && mkdir /working/OS && echo 'OS' > /working/OS/.theme && touch /working/workspace
